newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sipa shares slump on Mount Olympus data.
newsitem.headline: Sipa shares slump on Mount Olympus data.

text.p: Disappointing results from the Mount Olympus prospect in Western Australia devastated shares in gold explorer Sipa Resources International NL in morning trade on Friday, the stock plunging nearly 60 percent to 16 cents.
The company said metallurgical work on sulphide mineralisation from the prospect had shown that there was not an economic refractory ore treatment process available.

Sipa cited the high proportion of the contained gold as refractory, a lower than necessary ratio of gold to sulphur and active carbon species in the mineralisation as detracting from the project's economics. Contained gold that is refractory is not amenable to recovery by the conventional cyanidisation process treatment, it said.
"It came off in a big way after that announcement. It looks like they can't treat the ore economically," one analyst said.
"It means the ore won't surrender the gold easily," he added, noting that combined with the gold market slump the company had been dealt a double blow.
"They have a couple of other options but on top of the gold price fall, it has just wiped a lot of the company's market capitalisation away."
By 12.30 p.m. 90230 GMT), Sipa shares were 20.5 cents lower at 17.5 cents on turnover of 5.9 million shares.
